R6Q-bear-backcountry-0001.name: By Conglomerate Creek
R6Q-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R6Q-bear-backcountry-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Burn from 2023 (fire R90857), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SE facing slope, 15 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Conglomerate Creek 110 m E: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Northern Rockies Regional Municipality, about 489 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 57.26982, -128.91046, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 9.9 km NW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 321 m, about 229 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 220 m SE of the spot at 1,318 m (57.34833, -128.97911). Water: unnamed wetland 70 m E (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
